edges.description: Loss of GUCY2C tumor-suppressive signaling removes a brake on crypt proliferation, permitting adenoma-to-carcinoma progression.

nodes.description: Stepwise progression from adenomatous polyps to invasive carcinoma drives colon adenocarcinoma development.

evidence.reference_title: The adenoma carcinoma sequence in colorectal neoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Molecular studies support the clinical impression that adenocarcinoma of the large intestine develops in stages. At the center of the pathological continuum between normal mucosa and invasive carcinoma is the premalignant lesion, the adenomatous polyp.

nodes.description: Low-dose aspirin is an established chemopreventive ("interception") agent that reduces the recurrence of colorectal adenomas — the precursor lesions of colon adenocarcinoma. The cited randomized trial evaluated secondary prevention in higher-risk individuals with a recent history of documented adenomas; the 81 mg dose reduced adenoma recurrence while 325 mg did not. Its antineoplastic effect in the large bowel is attributed largely to inhibition of COX/prostaglandin-driven pro-tumorigenic signaling within the adenoma-carcinoma sequence. Preventive use is balanced against gastrointestinal bleeding risk.

evidence.reference_title: A randomized trial of aspirin to prevent colorectal adenomas.
evidence.snippet: We performed a randomized, double-blind trial of aspirin as a chemopreventive agent against colorectal adenomas.

nodes.description: Oral GUCY2C agonists (linaclotide, plecanatide) aim to reactivate the tumor-suppressive GUCY2C axis that is silenced early in colorectal carcinogenesis, restoring cGMP-dependent homeostatic signaling and restraining epithelial proliferation. In a human study oral linaclotide activated GUCY2C and reduced colorectal epithelial proliferation, but only after colon preparation — the FDA-approved gastric-release formulation does not reliably reach the colorectum, so a colorectum-targeted formulation is required before this can serve as a chemopreventive.

evidence.reference_title: Bioactivity of Oral Linaclotide in Human Colorectum for Cancer Chemoprevention.
evidence.snippet: The study results highlight the importance of developing a novel GUCY2C agonist formulated for release and activity targeted to the large intestine for colorectal cancer prevention

nodes.description: The intestinal receptor guanylyl cyclase C (GUCY2C) enforces epithelial homeostasis and restrains crypt proliferation. Early in colorectal carcinogenesis its endogenous hormones guanylin and uroguanylin are lost, silencing GUCY2C-cGMP signaling and removing a tumor-suppressive brake — a change that permits progression along the adenoma-carcinoma sequence and is the rationale for GUCY2C-agonist chemoprevention.

evidence.reference_title: Bioactivity of Oral Linaclotide in Human Colorectum for Cancer Chemoprevention.
evidence.snippet: Guanylate cyclase C (GUCY2C) is a tumor-suppressing receptor silenced by loss of expression of its luminocrine hormones guanylin and uroguanylin early in colorectal carcinogenesis.

nodes.description: MUC1 is an epithelial glycoprotein aberrantly expressed on colorectal adenomas and carcinomas, making it a candidate shared antigen for immunoprevention. A MUC1 peptide vaccine aims to raise anti-MUC1 immunity to intercept recurrent adenoma formation in individuals with a prior advanced adenoma. In a randomized, placebo-controlled prevention trial the vaccine was immunogenic only in vaccine recipients but did not significantly reduce adenoma recurrence overall; a 38% absolute reduction was seen in the subset who mounted an immune response. It remains investigational.

evidence.reference_title: Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of MUC1 Peptide Vaccine for Prevention of Recurrent Colorectal Adenoma.
evidence.snippet: An immune response was observed only in vaccine recipients.
